Kim / team / Gil — adding the technical detail that typically trips customers, plus an abbreviated compatibility checklist below. I also pasted an abbreviated matrix sample at the end.

Key patterns we support for private deployments:
- Splunk HEC (recommended when customer can accept a single TLS egress to 8088):
  - Auth: HEC token (bearer) or mTLS if using private HEC proxy
  - Ports: 8088 (HEC) over TLS; if you prefer syslog, see below
  - Agent: Fluent Bit / Splunk Universal Forwarder as an optional agent inside the VPC; Redwood can push via secure egress when configured
  - Notes: Token rotation supported; recommend <24h rotation policy for high-sensitivity customers

- Syslog over TLS (RFC 5425):
  - Auth: mTLS (recommended) or TCP TLS with cert validation
  - Ports: 6514 (syslog TLS)
  - Agent: syslog-ng / rsyslog as a local forwarder. Good for traditional SIEM pipelines.

- HTTPS event POST (Redwood event API / generic):
  - Auth: mTLS or bearer token + IP allowlist
  - Ports: 443 outbound
  - Agent: sidecar (Fluent Bit) or Redwood-managed forwarder when allowed

- OTLP traces (OpenTelemetry) — preferred for structured tracing hooks:
  - Auth: mTLS + token optional
  - Ports: 4317 (gRPC OTLP) or 55681 (HTTP OTLP)
  - Sampling: default 5-10% for production; can bump for high-fidelity debugging windows
  - Notes: We expose span-enrichment hooks (service.name, request.id) and can roll in KPIs for request latency that feed into your SIEM or APM.

Network & operational caveats:
- Egress proxy: If outbound TLS is restricted, a customer-managed egress proxy (mutual TLS) is the most straightforward path. Redwood supports proxy handshake with client certs; we recommend a short KMS-backed cert lifecycle and CRL/OCSP checking.
- NAT vs. static IP: For allowlisting, static egress IP or NAT range is required — we can publish a small set of IPs for dedicated deployments.
- Evidence chain: We can sign event batches with a rotating key and provide audit logs for certificate issuance/rotation to meet SOC-style evidence requests.

Short compatibility checklist (network team):
- Confirm target endpoint and accepted auth (HEC token / mTLS)
- Open outbound port to endpoint (8088 for HEC, 6514 for syslog TLS, 4317 for OTLP)
- Provide test credentials or CA bundles for mTLS test
- Confirm whether traffic must pass through corporate proxy and provide proxy credentials
- Confirm retention buckets and required metadata fields (timestamp, service, host, trace_id)

Matrix sample row (CSV style):
format,auth,port,agent,recommended_use,notes
Splunk-HEC,Token/mTLS,8088,Fluent Bit/UF,Log ingest,Token rotation; highest throughput
syslog-TLS,mTLS,6514,syslog-ng,Legacy SIEM,Prefer mTLS; store raw RFC5424 messages
OTLP,gRPC mTLS,4317,OpenTelemetry collector,Traces/Perf,Use for traces; sample 5-10%
